subject: Closure drift forensics and stitch plan
messages:
From: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@acme.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, DevOps Team <infra@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Timeline concern — go-live target slipping (MAP impact)

Logan —

Quick note from the ACME side: after our weekly engineering sync this morning it looks like the internal evaluation (security review and perf validation) will push the go-live from Jul 9 to Jul 23 unless we accelerate some checkpoints. The security team has one outstanding ask around audit log retention and an updated SOC-2 artifact we were expecting by EOW. Procurement also flagged a narrowed fiscal-window for Q3 allocation.

Can you propose a compacted MAP that buys us the current spend window but keeps risk controlled? If we need a short-term SLA concession to make the July 9 date plausible, flag what you need from procurement.

I attached the current MAP and the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lowe
Director, Platform Partnerships
Acme Enterprises

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), procurement_timeline.pdf (referenced)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline concern — go-live target slipping (MAP impact)

Sara —

Thanks for the flag and for sharing the MAP. I took a first pass and built a short plan to try to preserve Jul 9 while limiting exposure. High level:

- Narrowed acceptance gates: move perf soak to a post-canary window (day +7) and keep security gating for P0 items only (audit log retention is P1).
- Temporary operational SLOs: propose a 30-day SLA buffer (documented) that reduces penalty exposure while we finish SOC-2 artifacts.
- Deliverables: we can provide a compact evidence bundle (infra-evidence.zip) and a one-week focused runbook with the ACME DevOps team to accelerate verification.

What I need from Acme:
1) Procurement sign-off on a short-term SLA concession (we'll draft wording).
2) DevOps to agree to two 2-hour pairing sessions next week (for verifying KV retention and prefix caching behavior).
3) A named reviewer for the SOC-2 artifact (so we can target the exact missing evidence).

I attached a redline for the SLA (SLA_change_redline.docx) and an updated MAP snapshot that isolates must-have vs nice-to-have eval gates. If Jul 9 remains infeasible, we recommend a controlled rebaseline to Jul 23 with an interim canary on Jul 9 limited to 10% traffic and reduced throughput.

Would you and procurement be available for a quick call tomorrow to lock this?

—Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (updated snapshot), SLA_change_redline.docx, infra-evidence.zip

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline concern — go-live target slipping (MAP impact)

Looping in a couple notes from a risk and escalation perspective —

- Forensics summary (short): the drift looks driven by two separate bottlenecks: (A) audit-evidence turnaround from ACME's compliance team (P1), (B) ACME procurement window constraints. Neither is a technical blocker for a Jul 9 canary but both increase commercial exposure.
- Risk scoring: we've logged this as Risk-27 on the deal (moderate) and recommend the temporary SLA buffer + canary approach.
- Escalation play: if procurement cannot approve the concession by EOD Fri (2026-06-19), we will escalate to the enterprise sales leadership and recommend an immediate rebaseline to Jul 23.

Action items assigned:
- Sara / Acme procurement: confirm whether a 30-day SLA concession is acceptable (deadline: 2026-06-19 17:00 PDT).
- Karthik: prepare an internal note for leadership with cost delta for 30-day concession.
- Logan: schedule the two pairing sessions with ACME DevOps and prepare the canary roll plan (10% traffic, monitoring dashboard links).

I'll standby for procurement's reply. If we need to escalate, I will draft the exec note and loop the CRO.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Quoted message below:
> On Tue, 16 Jun 2026 at 09:07, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Sara —
> > 
> > Thanks for the flag and for sharing the MAP. I took a first pass and built a short plan to try to preserve Jul 9 while limiting exposure. ...

From: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com, DevOps Team <infra@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Timeline concern — go-live target slipping (MAP impact)

Marissa / Logan —

Thanks for the clear options and for doing the forensics. Procurement has reviewed the SLA redline and is willing to accept the 30-day, limited-scope concession provided the concession is strictly timeboxed and does not change payment terms. They asked for the concession wording and the canary cut plan in DocuSign by EOD Tue (2026-06-23).

DevOps confirmed two pairing sessions (June 24 & June 25 09:00–11:00 PT). SOC-2 reviewer is assigned: Priya Menon (priya.menon@acme.com).

Next steps agreed:
- Logan: finalize DocuSign wording for the temporary concession and share the canary runbook link.
- Karthik: send the internal cost delta to Marissa.
- Marissa: if procurement rescinds, escalate per the play.

If all goes per plan, ACME will proceed with a Jul 9 limited canary and full go-live on Jul 23. Appreciate the flexibility.

Best,
Sara

Attachments referenced: DocuSign request link (to be provided)
